_about: Scientific data library, domain ecology: the universal columns of the game's body/data/ecology.json tables, written by scripts/split_data.py. Same columns/rows schema as the game's tables. `id` is stable (see README); `source` holds source keys from sources.json ('; ' separated) or 'open'. Mark is the review state of these columns. A null in a column the engine's data/*.json holds by the same id means the engine file is the home of that value.

depletion_rules.title: Depletion and regeneration rules
depletion_rules.source: Logistic recovery is the Schaefer model's own; the catch-per-effort fall is the standard signal (CPUE proportional to B); the 'tragedy' row is the Cayman history.
rows: catch = q x effort x B / K (q from Fishing skill, FISHING.md stages); the minigame shows B/K as how many silhouettes appear
B += r B (1 - B/K) / 365 - today's catch (all boats on the ground, aggregate for distant ones)
B under 0.2 K: catch x0.2, the port's fish price up (economy), the fisherman duty yields little
logistic: from 0.2 K back to 0.8 K takes about 2.8/r years (reef fish 7 years, pelagics 3, turtles 56)
live turtles kept in pens do not deplete further but do not breed; a crawl of N feeds N x 30 kg
taking turtles on the beach in nesting season takes breeding females: r x0.5 for that stock for a decade
the same model for game; boucaniers on Hispaniola at MSY x3 drove cattle to near zero by 1700 (history)

soil.title: Soil fertility model
soil.source: A fertility index per field (0 to 1) drained by each crop's demand and restored by manure, fallow and legumes; Barbados exhaustion and the planters' manuring response are the historical anchor (ECO-SOIL). Numbers are placeholders.
rows: f -= demand (cane 0.06, tobacco 0.08, maize 0.03, cassava 0.01, pease -0.02 i.e. restores)
yield = max yield x (0.3 + 0.7 f) x rain factor x labour factor
f += 0.03 per 10 t/ha of dung (cattle pens next to cane fields: the Barbados practice)
f += 0.02 a year idle; +0.04 under bush
clearing forest gives f = 0.9 for a new field but removes firewood for the mill and raises erosion: f -= 0.02 a year extra on slopes
a dry year (under 60% of normal) halves yields; a hurricane destroys standing cane and plantains for a season
